where: Local Docker on the owner's laptop, not the cloud. Postgres 16; the API and webhook receiver as uv containers; k6 0.54.0 in a container on the same network. Not comparable one-to-one with docs/results/load-test-cloud-20261124*.json (different machine, no network hop).

setup.database: tpm_load, a copy of the local database migrated to 0017 (then 0018). Tenant demo: 391,486 events (Kubernetes v1.33-v1.38, Kafka 4.2.0-4.5.0, this repo). Tenant acme: a copy of the same 391,486 events and the same team configs (scripts/load/seed_second_tenant.py), so row-level security filters two equally large tenants.
setup.api_role: tpm_load_app, NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS, as the API connects on Cloud SQL. The local superuser bypasses RLS and would hide the cost.
setup.api: python -m api.main with WORKER_IN_PROCESS=true (the lean cloud shape, ADR-0017), AUTH_MODE=required; Redis database 5 so the existing local worker could not take the test's events.
setup.webhooks: collectors.github_webhooks with TPM_TENANT=demo; signed pull_request deliveries for kubernetes/kubernetes, PR numbers from 990000, title prefix LOADTEST-MARKER.

profile.reads: Same pages as 2026-11-24: /releases, /releases/v1.38/summary, /releases/v1.38/features, /releases/v1.38/dependencies, /releases/4.5.0/features, then 1 s sleep. Ramp to 10 users for 70 s, then 20 users for 70 s, per tenant.
profile.second_tenant: MODE=two: the same reads for acme, signed (signature v2, X-TPM-Tenant).
profile.burst: MODE=two: 20 webhooks/s for 30 s (600 deliveries) starting at 60 s.

bottleneck_found.what: The API's per-request 'any new events?' read (PostgresEventSource.load_after: id > last_id ORDER BY id) under row-level security walked the primary key past every newer row of the other tenant and filtered them out.
bottleneck_found.evidence: EXPLAIN ANALYZE as tpm_load_app, tenant demo: Index Scan using pk_events, Rows Removed by Filter: 391486, 557-773 ms. The tenant's max(id): 575 ms (backward pk scan, 391,486 rows removed).
bottleneck_found.fix: Migration 0018: index events (tenant_id, id), built concurrently. load_after first reads the tenant's max(id) (index-only scan, 0.7 ms) and returns at once when nothing is new; otherwise it reads the bounded range id > last_id AND id <= newest.
bottleneck_found.why_not_seen_before: One tenant in the cloud today: no other tenant's rows sit above the demo's last id. It appears as soon as a second tenant's events are written after the demo's.

1_demo_reads_before_fix.note: Code at main 4f5ceaf, two tenants in the database, only the demo reading. Idle cached pages took 0.19-0.51 s each (health 2 ms).

webhook_ingest.note: observed_at (receiver) to ingested_at (Postgres) for run 3. Event-to-dashboard push was not measured here; the cloud figure is docs/results/webhook-latency-cloud-20261124T044532Z.json.

isolation: 0 responses for acme contained the webhook marker in any run, and 0 marker events were stored under acme (600 under demo).
open_weak_spots: Tail stalls during recompute: with 40 readers and a burst, every page (including Kafka 4.5.0, which the burst does not touch) had a max of 11-15 s, and even /health took up to 2.08 s. The API sat at about one full core (108%): CPU-bound in one Python process (recompute threads, garbage collection). Burst alone or one reader alone: no stall (max 0.84 s). Not fixed in this PR; follow-up issue.

Memory per tenant: API memory 2.11 GiB with the demo warm, 3.84 GiB with both tenants warm (each tenant's ReleaseService keeps its whole event list and views). Cloud Run gives the API 4 GiB, so a third demo-sized tenant would not fit. Follow-up issue.
Cold start of a private tenant: only the demo is warmed at boot, so acme's first /releases took 47-49 s and its first v1.38 summary 28-32 s. Follow-up issue.
